more_info.overview: Enzyme-treated starch is food starch processed in water with one or more food-grade starch-breaking enzymes. JECFA describes treatment below the starch's gelatinisation temperature. The resulting preparation has technological thickening, stabilising, binding or emulsifying functions. It is distinct from a starch modified using a crosslinking or esterifying reagent. The commercial enzyme preparation and starting starch need to be identified separately from this broad process name.
more_info.origin: Plant starch processed in an aqueous medium with food-grade starch-breaking enzymes below its gelatinisation temperature. The botanical starch and enzyme source are not fixed by the generic name.
